implementerProof.how: Drove the same surface independently rather than re-running its script, which no longer exists: /tmp/infra-184/prove.sh lived on the implementer's container filesystem, and each role of this issue pod has its own. The rig was rebuilt from nothing on the issue volume (Debian postgresql-17 17.11 and postgresql-17-pgvector 0.8.0 downloaded with apt-get download and unpacked with dpkg-deb -x under /legion/scratch/harness/root, no root; initdb --locale-provider=icu --icu-locale=en-US; two packages/dispatch/e2e/run-server.sh servers, port 18877 from this branch and port 18878 from 7bf2759c6e17, each on its own database), and all four of its criteria and all of its negative controls were re-run on fresh fixtures with the branch CLI rebuilt from this head (packages/pi-envoy/dist/dispatch.js, bun run build). Every claim of its proof held: A1's sixth interleaved post recorded session_writes_since_human 2 with no cadence line (6 and 'Stop posting here until a human replies.' on the pre-change server); A2's sixth own post still printed the stop line; claim and release on legion, Legion and a child of a labelled parent named issue-update nowhere; the labelled triage comment and the labelled parent's triage child printed their comment id alone while recording issue_status=triage legion_managed_status=true, and the unlabelled control printed the line with legion_managed_status=false; doc-edit with no artifact edited the spec and --artifact spec reached the same document. Logs: /legion/scratch/harness/verify.log and /legion/scratch/harness/break2.log.

proof.criterion: A1 (R1). Three sessions post twice each on one issue. The write response to the sixth post reports two writes for its own session (session_writes_since_human), and the dispatch command prints no cadence line at all; the same run on the commit before the change reports six and prints "Stop posting here until a human replies."
proof.surface: The dispatch command an agent runs (this branch's CLI, packages/pi-envoy/dist/dispatch.js, rebuilt from this head) against two Dispatch servers started by packages/dispatch/e2e/run-server.sh on a real Postgres 17.11 with pgvector 0.8.0: port 18877 built from this branch, port 18878 built from 7bf2759c6e17, the commit before the change, each on its own database.
proof.command: bash /legion/scratch/harness/verify.sh, section A1: six dispatch message runs on TST-75 under three DISPATCH_SESSION_ID values (a1-one, a1-two, a1-three), each with its own DISPATCH_STATE_DIR, interleaved so the sixth is a1-three's second, then jq over that session's results.jsonl for details.advice.session_writes_since_human; the same six interleaved posts repeated on the pre-change server (TST-1 there).
proof.observed: The sixth run printed its message id alone and recorded session_writes_since_human = 2. No 'You've sent', no 'Progress ledger or scratchpad? If so, stop.', no 'Stop posting here until a human replies.'. 66 assertions, 0 failures in that run (/legion/scratch/harness/verify.log).

You've sent 6 messages on TST-1 with no human response. Stop posting here until a human replies.' — the miscount this issue fixes, reproduced live at the same moment.

proof.criterion: A2 (R1). Negative control: one session posts 6 times with no human event. Its last answer carries "Stop posting".
proof.surface: The same branch CLI against the branch server on port 18877.
proof.command: bash /legion/scratch/harness/verify.sh, section A2: six dispatch message runs on TST-76, all under DISPATCH_SESSION_ID=a2-solo, on an issue with no human event.

proof.criterion: A3 (R2), the claim and release half. A claim on an issue that carries legion, one that carries Legion, and one whose parent carries it, none of them name issue-update; nor does releasing a claim on them.
proof.surface: The same branch CLI against the branch server on port 18877, on ten issues created through the command itself: TST-77 (legion), TST-78 (Legion), TST-79 (LEGION), TST-81 (no label, parent TST-80 labelled legion), TST-84 (no label, two links below TST-82 labelled legion), TST-85 (label infra), TST-86 (label legionary).

A second claim by the holder (the no-op write path, where the server writes nothing and short-circuits) answered the same sentence.

A labelled issue claimed against the server built from 7bf2759c6e17 also still answered 'move it to in_progress with dispatch issue-update', so the client keeps today's wording against a server that answers no field — the rolling-deploy case.

proof.criterion: A3 (R2), the triage half. A comment on a triage issue carrying the label, and on a triage issue whose parent carries it, prints nothing about triage, and the advice that write recorded shows the issue in triage with Legion owning its status, so an absent line cannot be mistaken for absent advice. Negative control: the same comment on a triage issue with no such label prints "is still in triage" and its advice shows Legion does not own that status. Each comment is that session's first write on that issue.
proof.surface: The same branch CLI against the branch server on port 18877, on three triage issues: TST-87 (label legion), TST-89 (no label, parent TST-88 labelled legion), TST-90 (label infra). Each row ran under its own DISPATCH_SESSION_ID and its own DISPATCH_STATE_DIR, so each comment was that session's first write on that issue — the line shows once per issue per session and the command keeps that memory on disk (packages/envoy-client/src/dispatch-session-state.ts).
proof.command: bash /legion/scratch/harness/verify.sh, section A3 part 2: dispatch comment --issue <KEY> --body 'first write by <session>' per row, then jq over that session's results.jsonl for details.advice.issue_status and details.advice.legion_managed_status.
proof.observed: TST-87 recorded issue_status=triage legion_managed_status=true and printed its comment id and nothing else; TST-89, the child of a labelled parent, recorded the same and likewise printed only its comment id. Both assertions are positive as well as negative: the recorded advice proves the write was advised and the issue was in triage, so the missing line is the change and not a missing answer. dispatch message and dispatch ask on such an issue dropped the line too.
proof.negativeControl: TST-90, a triage issue with no legion label on it or above it, recorded issue_status=triage legion_managed_status=false and printed 'TST-90 is still in triage — nobody can see its development status. See the `dispatch` skill, "Issue status is yours to move".' The same first write on a labelled triage issue against the server built from 7bf2759c6e17 printed that line too, and its recorded advice carried no legion_managed_status at all, so the line's absence on this branch is the change and not the fixture.

proof.observed: The no-artifact edit applied and minted spec version 2; --artifact spec read the new text back; the following --artifact spec edit minted version 3, so both reached one document. A bare --ref dispatch://<KEY> reached the same document as version 4. This is the command skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md:114 shows, which was refused before.

breakAttempts: The client's once-per-issue memo: a session whose line was suppressed on a Legion issue is told 'is still in triage' as soon as another session takes the label off (the memo is marked inside the printing block), and a session that has already been told is not told twice. Both held; the first is the reason a proof must use one fresh session per row.

A person's write on a Legion-run triage issue (the rig's dev sign-in cookie, as a browser's; the agent bearer may act only as a session, ACTOR_KIND) still carries issue_status=triage and resolves no legion_managed_status, so the line stays for a reader who may move the status, and the early return outside the savepoint still fills the issue status.
A write on an issue past triage resolves the field not at all, so no parent walk runs where no line depends on it.
The walk is live, not stored: a legion label put on the parent after the child exists flips both the claim text and the triage line on the child.

The deepest descendant the tree allows — 32 links below a labelled root, the parentDepthCap boundary, a 33rd link refused by the server — still resolves legion_managed_status true on both the advice and the claim, so the walk's depth bound is not one short.
Two sessions posting at the same instant on one issue each counted only their own three.
A near-miss label (legionary) and an issue with no label on it or above it keep today's wording; the match is lower(label) = 'legion' and takes no prefix.
doc-edit given an inner ref (dispatch://<KEY>/message/<uuid>) is refused with a hint that now names the issue alone and no artifact slug, which is the command that would now work.
testsJudged: The implementer's tests would catch every way this broke under the attempts above. TestWriteAdviceCountsOnlyTheCallingSessionsOwnWrites pins the per-session count and the human reset; TestClaimAnswersWhoOwnsTheIssuesStatus pins both routes, the label in either case, a child of a labelled parent, and the no-op release short-circuit; TestWriteAdviceAnswersWhoOwnsTheIssuesStatus pins the advice's four rows and reads the raw JSON so an omitted field is told from a false one, which a typed decode cannot; the client tests pin the dropped line, the line on false, the unmarked memo, both claim answers, and doc-edit's default document; the contracts test pins the issue-without-artifact acceptance and the project-without-artifact refusal. Two cases hold only by the recursion in legionManagedStatusSQL and have no unit test: an ancestor two or more links up, and a label in a case other than legion or Legion. Both were driven live here (TST-84 two links below a labelled root; TST-79 labelled LEGION; TST-165 at the depth cap). A refactor that replaced the recursive CTE with a single parent lookup would pass the whole suite, so the reviewer may want that row; nothing is broken today, so no red test was written.
